svg.aria-label: Diagram: the SageMaker AI serverless customization sequence-length table, where each populated cell shows the maximum sequence length for one combination of model, customization technique and training type. An asterisk means the sequence length is fixed at 4K and not overridable; an em dash means the technique and training type are not supported for that model. The newly announced Muse Glimmer, Qwen3.8 27B and Ministral 3 models carry overridable values in every cell. The direction of the LoRA versus full fine-tuning difference reverses between rows: Muse Glimmer 30B is 32K for SFT with LoRA and 16K with full fine-tuning, while Nemotron 3 Nano 30B A3B is 8K for DPO with LoRA and 16K with full fine-tuning. Continuous customization requires the LoRA training type, which on some models is the lower ceiling. Customized open weight models deploy to SageMaker AI Inference endpoints while customized Nova models deploy to Amazon Bedrock.
svg.title: The ceiling belongs to the cell, not to the model
svg.text: One cell per model, per technique, per training type. They disagree.
SageMaker AI serverless model customization — Muse Glimmer, Qwen3.8 27B, Ministral 3 3B / 8B / 14B.
A cell carries one of three things, and only one of them is a ceiling
16K / 32K a maximum you can set under → “you can set any value up to that ceiling”
*4K “fixed at 4K and is not overridable” → the parameter does not apply here
— “not supported for serverless customization on that model”
LoRA higher — Muse Glimmer 30B, SFT
SFT (LoRA) 32K
SFT (FFT) 16K
Twice the budget on the low-rank path.
huggingface-vlm-muse-glimmer-30b
LoRA lower — Nemotron 3 Nano 30B, DPO
DPO (LoRA) 8K
DPO (FFT) 16K
Same table. Opposite direction.
So “LoRA allows more context” has a counter-example.
The techniques do not rank consistently either
Ministral 3 3B SFT/DPO 16K both types · RLVR/RLAIF 32K both types → reinforcement is the longer one
Qwen3.8 27B SFT/DPO 16K both types · RLVR/RLAIF 16K LoRA, 8K FFT → reinforcement is where it halves
Which leaves one safe procedure: look up the exact combination you are about to run.
What the budget covers
“the sum of the prompt length and the response
length, and you set them independently”
SFT, DPO dataset_max_len
RLVR, RLAIF max_prompt_length +
max_response_length
Two documented facts that interact
Continuous customization chains SFT → DPO → RLVR
and “Requires LoRA training type.”
On a row where LoRA is the lower cell, chaining has
also chosen the shorter budget for that step.
Reading the two pages together; neither says it.
And the customized model does not land where a Nova customization lands.
“The deployment path depends on the model type.” Nova → Amazon Bedrock. Open weight → SageMaker AI Inference
endpoints — which is where these three families land, and a different surface to secure.
Available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Tokyo) and Europe (Ireland).
